findings.title: resetDb is not serialised: a reset that outlives its hook timeout races the next test's reset, turning one slow test into a cascade of unrelated failures
findings.evidence: resetDb() runs terminate -> DROP DATABASE -> CREATE DATABASE … TEMPLATE with no per-process mutex (unlike ensureWorkerDb, which shares one `ready` promise, db.ts:66-71). When vitest gives up on a beforeEach after hookTimeout 30 s, the abandoned resetDb keeps running; the next test's beforeEach starts a second resetDb on the same DB name. Baseline 2026-10-31 (baseline/backend-test.log:285-299, 345-346): 16 of the 44 failures are exactly this — 14 x `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "pg_database_datname_index"` and 2 x `database "postgres_87470_mvwu62uq_w8|w1" already exists`, each in the test right after a hook timeout in the same file. The same orphaned work explains the uncaught `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'write')` in postgres.js (log, Unhandled Errors, po-sold-lifecycle) and the CONNECTION_CLOSED/ENDED/CONNECT_TIMEOUT "Unhandled error" log lines (log:147, 241): the next reset terminates/ends pools that a timed-out test is still using. Repro: docs/review-2026-10-31/repro/A2t/reset-cascade.repro.test.ts abandons one resetDb() after 5 ms and the following test fails with the identical pg_database_datname_index error, 3/3 runs.
findings.failure_scenario: A loaded CI runner or a dev box running two suites (the release gate racing a local run, which global-setup.ts was written for) slows one reset past 30 s; instead of one timeout the file reports a timeout plus N "database already exists"/unhandled-error failures in unrelated tests, and vitest flags "This might cause false positive tests". The 44-failure baseline reads like 20 broken files when none is broken, so real regressions hide in the noise and people learn to rerun until green.
findings.proposed_fix: Chain resetDb onto a module-level promise (`let resetting = Promise.resolve(); export function resetDb(){ return resetting = resetting.catch(()=>{}).then(doReset); }`) so a second call waits for the first, and make the CREATE tolerate an existing clone by DROP … WITH (FORCE) immediately before it. Optionally raise hookTimeout or make resetDb time-boxed with AbortSignal so an abandoned reset cannot outlive its test.
findings.regression_test: docs/review-2026-10-31/repro/A2t/reset-cascade.repro.test.ts (run with its vitest.repro.config.ts) must pass after the fix; it fails 3/3 today.

findings.title: wave2b Fix 3b and Fix 3c pass whatever the PO back-advance guard does; the "Done sell order frees the line" branch is untested
findings.evidence: Fix 3b (245-255) creates no sell order at all, so "forward advance is not blocked even with lines on sell orders" only tests a plain reviewing -> done. Fix 3c (257-284) moves done -> reviewing, a move Fix 3a (204-208) shows returns 200 even with an Awaiting-payment sell order on the line; the guard only bites at -> in_transit (209-216). The sell-order status calls at 274-277 are unchecked, so the SO may never reach Done.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression that makes the back-advance guard count Done sell orders as open commitments (blocking a legitimate PO revert to In Transit) or that stops checking commitments on forward moves passes both tests.
findings.proposed_fix: Fix 3b: attach an open sell order to a line before advancing forward. Fix 3c: assert each SO status call is 200, then advance done -> reviewing -> in_transit and expect 200.
findings.regression_test: Mutate the guard to treat Done SOs as open; Fix 3c must fail.

findings.title: Goods-total tests pass vacuously: the 0-to-NULL test starts at NULL and four "leave it alone" tests never check their PATCH succeeded
findings.evidence: line() (line 25) sets no sellPrice, so sell_price is already NULL before the PATCH at 384-386 sends sellPrice: 0; the final toBeNull() holds even if the API stores 0 or ignores the field. The "leaves it alone" tests (e.g. 115 `await api('PATCH', … { notes })` with no status check) assert the total did not move, which a 400/409/500 also satisfies.
findings.failure_scenario: A route change that rejects notes-only PATCHes, or that writes 0 into sell_price (breaking the constraint the comment at 377-378 says the API never trips), leaves the suite green.
findings.proposed_fix: Price the line first (as inventory.test.ts:148 does) and assert each PATCH status is 200.
findings.regression_test: Make the PATCH return 400; the four tests must fail.

findings.title: Tests titled with "no writes"/"keeps X"/"unchanged" never check the mutation was attempted or that the named fields stayed
findings.location: apps/backend/tests/orders.test.ts:484-507; orders.test.ts:589-612; inventory.test.ts:390-408; item-types.test.ts:133-143; order-box-checks.test.ts:234-241; transfer-orders.test.ts:408-419,624-636; sellOrder-price-adjust.test.ts:306; wave2b-fixes.test.ts:111-118; suppliers-adopt.test.ts:53-56; orders-on-behalf.test.ts:160-178
findings.evidence: orders.test.ts:504-506 fetches commissionRate and totalCost after the 409s but asserts only lines[0].qty. orders.test.ts:592 and 608 PATCHes are unchecked and the expected values (0, null) are the defaults. inventory.test.ts:399 PATCH unchecked and 406 allows before+1 events although the title says "writes no event". order-box-checks.test.ts:236 PUT unchecked and never shown stored before the DELETE. transfer-orders "409 (no writes)" check only transfer_orders.status, not the line's warehouse/status/transfer_order_id. suppliers-adopt.test.ts:53 uses find(...)! then ignores the adopt status.
findings.failure_scenario: A 409 that still commits commission_rate or total_cost (partial write before the refusal), or a line edit that moves a line's warehouse while returning 409, passes these tests.
findings.proposed_fix: Assert every setup/subject request status; assert every field the title names (commissionRate, totalCost, line warehouse/status); compare event counts with toBe(before) where the title promises none.
findings.regression_test: Inject a write before the 409 return in the PATCH handler; orders.test.ts:484 must fail.

findings.title: Negative-only scoping/filter tests have no positive control, so an endpoint that returns nothing passes
findings.evidence: Each asserts an empty/absent result (toEqual([]), includes()===false, .some()===false) without first showing a manager/unfiltered call returns the row. orders-handoff 593-611 seeds no bank_transactions, so "links nothing" holds by construction; orders-paypal-link-follows-id 76-78 never shows the PO was linked before clearing.
findings.failure_scenario: A broken q filter, a purchaser-scoping bug that hides rows from everyone, or a PayPal link that never links leaves these green while users see empty pages.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the positive half (manager sees it / unfiltered list contains it / linked before unlink) before each negative assertion.
findings.regression_test: Make the endpoint return [] unconditionally; each test must fail.

findings.title: Lock-wait race tests rely on a fixed 300 ms sleep instead of waiting for the blocked backend
findings.evidence: pause(300) stands in for "the request is now waiting on the lock". If the request reaches Postgres only after release() commits (slow runner, the 2026-10-31 baseline ran ~80x slower than normal), it sees the committed raise and refuses with the same 409/400, so the test passes with FOR UPDATE removed. review-lock-protocol.test.ts already has waitBlocked() polling pg_stat_activity/pg_locks for this.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone drops the row lock in the PO line-removal/archive path; under load the race tests still pass, and the oversell/strand bug they guard ships.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace pause(300) with the waitBlocked() helper (move it to tests/helpers) and assert the request was observed waiting before release().
findings.regression_test: Remove FOR UPDATE in the guarded path; test must fail deterministically, not only on fast machines.

findings.title: Count/metric assertions too weak to catch the regression they name
findings.evidence: ref-price-events asserts count >= 2 but seed.mjs inserts 12 events per ref_price, so a second appendPriceEvent that inserts nothing passes. metrics/observability "increments" tests match any counter value (\d+) with no before/after delta (observability.test.ts:110-146 does it correctly). order-serials asserts events.length > 0, which the create event alone satisfies.
findings.failure_scenario: appendPriceEvent stops writing history, or a metric stops incrementing, and the suite stays green.
findings.proposed_fix: Read the count before and assert toBe(before + n).
findings.regression_test: Make appendPriceEvent a no-op; ref-price-events must fail.

findings.title: Vacuous loops and silent early returns over possibly-empty results
findings.evidence: pagination asserts length <= 3 and loops over page B with no length check (78 compares createdAt strings, accepting ties). activity.test.ts:142 filters ?action=moved but the seed writes no transferred event, so the loop never runs. transfer-orders.test.ts:144/526 `if (!b) return;` and 764 `if (prior?.s) expect(...)` skip the assertion when data is missing. stock-lock-order.test.ts:28 `r.total === null ||`.
findings.failure_scenario: A cursor bug that returns an empty second page, or an action filter that drops inventory events, passes.
findings.proposed_fix: Assert non-empty (toBeGreaterThan(0)) before each loop; replace silent returns with expect(b).toBeDefined().
findings.regression_test: Make page 2 return []; pagination tests must fail.

findings.title: Wall-clock and calendar dependence in assertions
findings.evidence: input-bounds-redos asserts < 200 ms for 1000 regex runs on real time; attachment-image-shrink computes TODAY (UTC) once at module load and compares to server-dated filenames at 168; suppliers derives expected dates from Date.now() in UTC.
findings.failure_scenario: Flakes on a loaded runner (the baseline ran 80x slower) or when a run crosses UTC midnight; the ReDoS budget tests can fail spuriously, training people to rerun.
findings.proposed_fix: Use vi.useFakeTimers/vi.setSystemTime for dates; for ReDoS, assert step counts or use a generous budget relative to a baseline measured in the same test.
findings.regression_test: Run with TZ and system time set to 23:59:59.900 UTC; tests must stay green.

findings.title: part-merge test can pass without the migration rewriting any line
findings.evidence: The RAM line is inserted with RAM_USCORE and the expected value is whatever ref_prices row won (138-141); line 102 accepts either spelling as winner. If the tie-break picks the spelling the line already carries, ram.part_number === winner.part_number with zero rewrites.
findings.failure_scenario: A migration change that stops re-spelling RAM lines passes this test whenever the line already uses the winning spelling.
findings.proposed_fix: Seed the RAM line with the spelling that must lose (assert winner != original first), then assert it changed.
findings.regression_test: Delete the UPDATE order_lines step from the merge SQL; test must fail.

findings.title: sell-order PO line number assertions compare null to null
findings.evidence: Nothing asserts product_no is non-null or distinct; if inserted rows got NULL, noOf() returns null everywhere and every toBe(noOf(id)) and the sort check pass.
findings.failure_scenario: A trigger regression (0169) that stops assigning product_no leaves the test green.
findings.regression_test: Drop the BEFORE INSERT trigger in a test DB; test must fail.

findings.title: /api/client-timings has no test
findings.evidence: No file under apps/backend/tests references /api/client-timings (grep). Its auth gate, 20/min rate limit and loadEvent validation are untested; every other /api mount has at least one test.
findings.failure_scenario: A refactor of index.ts drops the authMiddleware lines for this mount; unauthenticated clients can then write arbitrary log lines (userEmail would throw, giving a 500 log flood) and nothing fails.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a small test: 401 without cookie, 400 without loadEvent, 204 on valid body, 429 after 20.

notes: Baseline classification: all 44 failures (20 files) are load artefacts, none a real failure. 28 are 15 s test / 30 s hook timeouts (baseline Duration 1215 s vs ~15 s normal: the machine was saturated by parallel review lanes); the other 16 are the A2t-01 reset race firing in the test after each timeout. Every one of the 20 files passed alone on my own PG18 (review1031-A2t, 127.0.0.1:55621; 328/328 tests) and all 20 together at 8 forks twice (328/328, ~55 s each, load avg 11). Per-file verdicts in baseline_failures. The 4 fixtures (jpeg/pdf) were listed not inspected byte-wise; the 140 test files were read by three sub-readers with their top claims spot-verified by me (wave2b 3b/3c, order-goods-total, orders.test 484/589, ref-price-events, part-merge, race pauses, inventory 390, order-box-checks 234); lower-ranked items in A2t-04..A2t-11 location lists are reader-reported and not each re-verified. Static scan found no it.skip/only/todo. Per-file process.env mutations were not flagged: the forks pool runs each file in a fresh process. Not checked: frontend tests, tracker suites, CI workflow behaviour beyond backend-tests.yml env. Container review1031-A2t removed at the end.
